clue.text: Got a first of course

parts.note: reads like earning a top university degree, but a course is also a racecourse, where coming first is what a backed horse does

explanation.walkthrough: A 'first' sounds like a top degree class at a British university; here the course is a racecourse and the first is the horse that wins.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a punter who bet on the race winner has had their horse come home first on the course.

clue.text: A rising of workers

parts.note: sounds like a revolt by labourers, but the workers are worker insects and the rising is a mound of earth they build

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' suggests an uprising or strike; here it is a small hill, and the workers are ants.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: a mound of earth raised by worker insects, a little rise of ground made by the colony.

clue.text: Work with stitches to heal

definitions.meaning: to make fabric by looping yarn with needles
broken bones mend by joining together again

explanation.surface: A doctor's wound repaired by sewing it up so that it can recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: making a garment from wool with needles, and broken bones growing back together.

clue.text: Sail had to be put up for these blooming things

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the words up means reading their letters from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards

explanation.surface: A sailor had to hoist the sail for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns SAILHAD backwards in this down clue. 'Blooming' looks like a mild British expletive but is literal: these things bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these are garden flowers, plants that are in bloom, so they are blooming things.

clue.text: Paw one's damagePaws one damaged which could be used in self-defenced that's used in self-defence

indicators.note: something damaged is broken out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal's injured foot is something it could protect itself with.
explanation.walkthrough: The stored clue repeats itself in several drafts; the parse uses 'Paws one damaged ... used in self-defence'. 'damaged' rearranges PAWSONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms such as guns or knives are things a person may use to protect themselves from attack.

clue.text: Return article if too unsophisticated

indicators.note: to return something is to send it back, so the word for the article is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone who sends back a purchase is thought too green to keep it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns AN into NA. 'too' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a naive, artless person or attitude is innocent and lacks worldly sophistication.

clue.text: Member of clergy leaves Apocalypse in state of euphoria

indicators.note: the clergyman's title departs, so it is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: Revelation is the biblical book also called the Apocalypse
Rev is short for Reverend, a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A priest walks out of a doom-laden sermon, leaving the congregation joyful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes REV from the start of REVELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: great happiness and exhilaration, a feeling of high spirits.

clue.text: The time it takes for ill-feeling to disappear

definitions.text: The time it takes for ill-feeling to disappear

parts.words: The time it takes for ill-feeling to disappear
parts.note: sounds like resentment fading, but ill-feeling is literally feeling ill, and the time is the period of recovery

explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-feeling' usually means animosity; here it is sickness, which goes away during recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: the period of gradual recovery after illness, until the patient no longer feels unwell.

clue.text: Looking or just thinking about it

definitions.meaning: considering doing something without yet doing it

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing a decision without committing to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: regarding something at length with the eyes, and merely considering an action as a possibility.

clue.text: No way to get wealthy — you'll just get the bird

parts.note: O is nought, zero, nothing
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A cynic warns there is no route to riches; you'll only be jeered, 'get the bird' being slang for being booed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' is British slang for being hissed at by an audience; here the bird is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large flightless African creature with feathers is one kind of bird.

clue.text: A giddy goat, it may be musically excited

indicators.note: giddy means dizzy and reeling, so these letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: A dizzy goat could be excited enough to dance to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giddy' rearranges AGOATIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical direction: the Italian marking telling a performer to play in an agitated, restless manner.

clue.text: One in front gets conceited

indicators.note: the numeral for one sits inside the word for the front

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person who pushes to the front is seen as full of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: VAN means the leading part, as in vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having too high an opinion of one's own looks or abilities.

clue.text: One's husband's late

parts.note: sounds like someone whose spouse is running behind time, but late here means deceased

explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like tardy; it means dead, as in 'the late Mr Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: a woman whose spouse has died and who has not remarried.

clue.text: Suggest a clue for this answer

definitions.meaning: a clue is a small pointer helping someone find a solution

explanation.surface: A solver asks for help with this very entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to indicate something indirectly, and a helpful pointer towards a solution.

clue.text: Virtuous but losing out over poisonous influence

indicators.note: the good word loses some letters, so they are taken away
in a down clue, over means turned upwards, so the word out is read backwards

explanation.surface: Being good, but missing out, puts one under a toxic sway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns OUT into TUO, and 'losing' removes TUO from VIRTUOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a harmful, corrupting thing that spreads, like an infection.

clue.text: Untie tricky knot

definitions.note: used as a verb: to tie together

indicators.note: tricky suggests something awkward and twisted, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Undoing a difficult knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges UNTIE; the surface sense of untying is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tie or join things together into one.

clue.text: Sell oil, rum and sticky sweets

indicators.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange, so these letters come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's stock list: oil, rum and confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the British adjective for odd, rearranging SELLOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: British term: sugary confections on sticks, lollipops, which are notoriously sticky.

clue.text: Term very much like another

parts.note: a word whose meaning closely matches that of a different word

explanation.walkthrough: Plain description of a word that means nearly the same as another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition: a word or phrase with the same or nearly the same meaning as another.

clue.text: Something that's essential when around fruit

indicators.note: turned around, so the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a must is something essential
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something vital happens whenever fruit is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns AMUSTAS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small, easily peeled citrus like a mandarin is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: One under instruction to make a stand about wet weather

indicators.note: the stand goes round, about, the weather word

parts.note: a tee is a small peg on which a golf ball stands
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A learner makes a protest about the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a stand' is the little peg a golfer rests the ball on before driving; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an apprentice, someone being taught a job, is under instruction.

clue.text: Ian came to dance looking pale and sickly

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ian turned up at the dance looking unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dance' rearranges IANCAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking red blood cells and so wan and weak in appearance.

clue.text: Acid criticism

definitions.meaning: the old name for sulphuric acid
bitter, caustic abuse or harsh words

explanation.surface: Biting, harsh comment.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the old term for sulphuric acid, and savagely bitter criticism.

clue.text: He composed valid styles for entertaining quartet

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece takes the other inside
to style something is to shape it anew, so the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A composer writes a quartet in respectable styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'styles' gives VALDI, and 'entertaining' takes the Roman four in after the first letter. 'quartet' looks musical, fitting the composer, but is just a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Venetian baroque composer of The Four Seasons is one man who composed.

clue.text: Complaint made by one head about learners

indicators.note: the first pieces go round, about, the learners

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a ness is a headland
L is the learner plate letter, so two learners are LL

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a headteacher concerning pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland (Loch Ness aside, as in Orford Ness); 'about' puts LL into INESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical sense: a complaint is an ailment or disorder, a sickness.

clue.text: Dutch product manufactured to be sent west

indicators.note: in an across clue, sending westward means reading right to left, i.e. backwards

parts.note: made means manufactured

explanation.surface: Goods manufactured in Holland for export.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sent west' turns MADE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a round cheese with red wax rind from the Netherlands is a Dutch product.

clue.text: Grub is right at the centre of burning issue

indicators.note: the letter for right is placed in the middle of the other word

parts.note: lava is molten rock that issues, burning, from a volcano

explanation.surface: Food is central to a heated debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning issue' looks like a hot topic; it is literally lava pouring out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a grub is an insect in its immature, wormlike stage.

clue.text: Residence with no outstanding features

definitions.meaning: a home, an apartment on one floor

explanation.surface: A dull, characterless home.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a set of rooms forming a home, and smooth and level with nothing protruding.

clue.text: House cover

parts.note: sounds like insurance for a home, but means the structure covering the top of a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' suggests insurance cover; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: the structure on top of a building that covers and shelters it.

clue.text: Work of art and one fake

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a con is a swindle or fake

explanation.surface: A painting that is also a forgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a religious painting on wood in the Orthodox tradition is a work of art.

clue.text: Agree to read in front of class

indicators.note: the reading word comes ahead of the class word

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Pupils consent to read aloud before their schoolmates.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old word meaning to study; FORM is a British school year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to comply or fit in with rules or others' views.

clue.text: An upholder of the Christian word

definitions.text: An upholder of the Christian word

parts.words: An upholder of the Christian word
parts.note: sounds like a defender of the faith, but is literally a stand that holds up the Bible

explanation.walkthrough: 'upholder' suggests a champion of doctrine; it is a stand that physically holds up the Bible in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: a reading desk in a church on which the Bible rests for readings.

clue.text: One prefers things not so-so, but just so

definitions.text: One prefers things not so-so, but just so

parts.words: One prefers things not so-so, but just so
parts.note: someone who rejects the mediocre and wants everything exactly right

explanation.walkthrough: Plays on 'so-so' (mediocre) and 'just so' (exactly right).
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a person who demands flawlessness and cannot accept anything less.
